column3: The Hebrew says “in the days of David” and “the house of bloodshed”; BSB uses “during the reign of David” and speaks of blood shed by Saul and his family.
The Hebrew calls the speaker “the king”; BSB names David.
Close to the Hebrew.
The Hebrew says that they have no man to put to death in Israel; BSB addresses David directly as the person who should not put anyone to death for them.
Close to the Hebrew.
The Hebrew says “sons”; BSB uses “male descendants.”
Close to the Hebrew.
The Hebrew names Michal; BSB names Merab.
The Hebrew uses singular “the hand of the Gibeonites”; BSB has plural “the hands”.
The Hebrew says “water” poured from heaven “on them”; BSB specifies “rain” and “the bodies.”
Close to the Hebrew.
The Hebrew explicitly names David and repeats “the Philistines”; BSB uses pronouns in those places.
The Hebrew has a separate active plural clause saying that they gathered the bones of those hanged; BSB combines those bones with the ones David had brought.
The Hebrew says that God was entreated for the land; BSB supplies the explicit phrase “answered their prayers.”
Close to the Hebrew.
The Hebrew says that he was girded with a “new” item, leaving the noun implicit; BSB supplies “sword.”
The Hebrew addresses David as the one who might extinguish Israel’s lamp; BSB expresses the extinguishing passively.
Close to the Hebrew.
The Hebrew names Jaare-oregim and says that Elhanan struck Goliath; BSB names Jair and supplies “the brother of Goliath.”
Close to the Hebrew.
Close to the Hebrew.
The Hebrew repeats “by the hand” for David and his servants; BSB combines them under one phrase.
